title: Barrier-free Access on Public Footpaths for Mobility Scooters and Motorised Wheelchairs
what_it_is: Barrier-free Access on Public Footpaths for Mobility Scooters and Motorised Wheelchairs

sections.label: Footpath width and encumbrances
sections.summary: Public paths are kept free of encumbrances, new footpaths must meet minimum widths, and old footpaths are widened unless site constraints exist.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Public paths are designed to be free from encumbrances to ensure a barrier-free passage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Since 2018, all new standalone footpaths are also required to have a minimum clear width of 1.8 metres, while those adjacent to cycling paths must be at least 1.5 metres.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: When rejuvenating old footpaths, we will widen them to these standards, unless there are site constraints, such as the lack of roadside space.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) also takes in residents' feedback when planning for footpath widening within private estates, which is often undertaken in conjunction with other programmes, such as drainage or estate improvements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Acting Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: If riders need to use the road briefly to bypass obstructions or access adjoining paths, enforcement authorities will exercise discretion.

sections.label: Path widening constraints in private estates
sections.summary: Path widening is usually done with other estate improvement works, faces constraints in private estates, and follows a calibrated approach based on user volume.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: As mentioned earlier, such path widening work is usually taken in conjunction with other estate improvement works, for example, drainage or estate improvements and these are not entirely within LTA's jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We really have to bear in mind the constraints in private estates, because you have trees, utilities and it is not so straightforward as in other places.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We do take a calibrated approach, looking at the volume of users – whether motorists on the roads or pedestrians and riders on the footpaths.
